set.body:
Current release queue, 7 October 2026: release-1.0; milestone-workspace.
Plan: docs/refactor/RELEASE-QUEUE.md. Mote remains authoritative; one primary agent and at most one helper.

Reconciliation: M1 fixture serializers/export components and qualified consumer exist; a fixture-generated archive is not ordinary-file CLI completion. Non-public recall use now makes the recorded typed disclosure-basis condition applicable.

Remaining / next action: Connect prepare and facade to one reusable Atlas-openable public study workflow. Reuse canonical M1 roles/joins, validate resume and atomic completion, and hand untouched output to the exact-pair Atlas consumer.

Release tags schedule work; they do not establish completion or empirical qualification. Use current AGENTS.md for ownership, scoped gates and exact-SHA review; old fleet roles, timers and fixed gate task counts are historical. Keep the original scientific preregistration, denominators, admission and sealed-test rules below.

Retained acceptance and design context:

Owner requirement: a researcher must be able to use StoryModel to create the actual source/recall/mapping artifacts accepted by StoryAtlas, starting from ordinary files. Governing docs/plans/2026-09-22-recall-encoding-workflow.md section 8 and sibling storyatlas4s/docs/delivery/workspace-design.md section 8.0.

Reuse and scope: orchestrate the existing public mapping facade and new ordinary-file preparation over the canonical M1 manifest/join/codec/writer. This is the reusable producer entry point; do not implement another estimator, require normal users to import embed-bench, or make them hand-edit JSON. Keep view generation/HTML in StoryAtlas.

Acceptance:
1. Document one entry workflow (study validate/run with a small config or equivalent public CLI) that prepares a source, prepares a cohort and writes an Atlas-openable investigation. Command spellings in plans are proposals until the real CLI is tested. Record exact installation/runtime/model/provider setup; reuse the existing release/distribution work rather than promise an unbuilt installer.
2. Prepare/cache the source once across at least two recalls and later additions. Resolve explicit unitization/evidence/inference/decision profiles once; separately label reference/reconstruction/unknown provenance as actually supported. Emit every unit and participant outcome; optional times/media do not become prerequisites for text inspection.
3. Publish canonical workspace manifest and required source/model, recall inventory, mapping, derivation/provenance and capability roles, with exact joins/digests and optional features/media bindings. Reuse packet schemas/serializer rather than inventing a second bundle. The inspector, subset and saved-state reader see the same records.
4. Resume validates input/profile/provider/output identity, keeps attempt-scoped failures, preserves completed participants and publishes atomically or with completion manifest last. Interrupted/corrupt/foreign output is rejected. Altering source or segmentation creates new identity rather than mutating historical investigations.
5. Run raw text plus two untimed recalls and an admitted annotation-assisted video case through the public workflow. Independent decode/readback verifies exact identities, units, support, values, outcomes and receipts. Hand the untouched output, exact CLI commands and artifact digests to Atlas consumer ticket bd-01M35AX3TA97BRYF29Z21RX6EF (foreign reference only). Actual Atlas opening must be qualified there; producer codec success does not assert a browser pass.
6. Keep annotation-assisted scope distinct from compiled-film automation and the full G2 organization/readout preview. This base artifact-creation path does not wait for imaging, general chronology, calibrated temporal precision or every analysis readout, and it is not an added prerequisite for M1 fixture-packet delivery.

Evidence: exact revisions/config/generator commands/fixtures, independent answers, interrupted-run and wrong-identity mutants with controls, documented user walkthrough, SD6 review, reference-scope and applicable checkAll gates. Report actual capability readiness separately from execution completion. Fallback is the existing checked source/recall entry; no silent WOG/sample replacement or unknown-schema downgrade.
